# `Q-2-1` — Unclosed Span

> A bracketed span or link begins with `[` but no closing `]`
> appears before the end of the block.

## What this means

Square brackets in Quarto markdown open one of several inline
constructs: a link, a citation, a bracketed span. The parser
expects every `[` to be balanced by a matching `]` within the
same paragraph or block. This error fires when the closing
bracket never appears.

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **A literal `[` you intended as text.** Outside of links and
  spans, a left bracket should be escaped as `\[`.
- **A typo that consumed the closing bracket.** The bracket may
  have been deleted in a recent edit but its open form left
  behind.
- **An unintended line break inside the construct.** Many
  bracketed constructs do not survive a paragraph boundary.

## How to fix

Add the closing `]` at the intended end of the construct. If you
meant the `[` literally, escape it with a backslash:

```markdown
A literal \[bracket\] in prose.
```

## Example

The parser reports the error on input like:

```markdown
an [unclosed span
```
